note: Game trading regions. `parentSea` names the sea a region is most identified with (an id from data/seas.json); ports inside a region may sit on other seas. Regions are an editorial game-design grouping, not an official geographic taxonomy.

regions.name: Iberia
regions.blurb: Portugal and Spain, the twin crowns whose Atlantic and Indies monopolies opened the ocean world after 1492.

regions.name: Atlantic Isles
regions.blurb: Madeira, the Azores, the Canaries and Cape Verde: sugar islands and the watering stations of every ocean crossing.

regions.name: British Isles
regions.blurb: England, Scotland and Ireland, exporting cloth, tin and coal and fishing the Newfoundland banks.

regions.name: France & the Low Countries
regions.blurb: The Channel and North Sea coasts, from Bordeaux wine to the Amsterdam exchange that financed the VOC.

regions.name: Baltic & the Hanse
regions.blurb: Grain, timber, tar and hemp from the eastern shores, gathered by Hanseatic and Dutch ships past the Sound toll.

regions.name: Scandinavia & the Arctic
regions.blurb: Stockfish, copper and train oil from Norway, Iceland, the Faroes and the Russian White Sea.

regions.name: Western Mediterranean
regions.blurb: Genoa, Marseille, Naples and the grain islands of Sicily, Sardinia and Malta.

regions.name: Adriatic & Ionian
regions.blurb: Venice, Ragusa and the Dalmatian and Greek harbours through which Balkan goods reached the sea.

regions.name: Aegean, Anatolia & Black Sea
regions.blurb: The Ottoman heartland seas: Istanbul, Smyrna, Crete and the Black Sea grain and fur ports.

regions.name: Levant & Egypt
regions.blurb: Alexandria, Beirut and Tripoli, the Mediterranean end of the caravan roads from Aleppo, Persia and the Red Sea.

regions.name: Maghreb
regions.blurb: Morocco, Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli: sugar, wax and hides, and the corsair fleets of the Barbary regencies.

regions.name: West Africa
regions.blurb: Senegambia to Angola: the gold of Mina, ivory, pepper and the fortified factory coast.

regions.name: East Africa & the Horn
regions.blurb: The Swahili city-states, the Zimbabwe gold outlets, the incense coast, and the Cape refreshment station.

regions.name: Arabia & the Gulf
regions.blurb: The Red Sea pilgrimage and coffee ports, Hormuz, and the pearl banks of the Persian Gulf.

regions.name: Western India
regions.blurb: Gujarat, the Konkan and Malabar: cotton cloth and indigo from Surat, pepper and cinnamon from Cochin.

regions.name: Eastern India, Ceylon & Burma
regions.blurb: Coromandel painted cottons, Bengal saltpetre and muslin, Ceylon cinnamon and Pegu rubies.

regions.name: Southeast Asia
regions.blurb: Malacca, Java, Siam and the Moluccas, where the world's only clove, nutmeg and mace grew.

regions.name: China Coast
regions.blurb: Canton, Macau, Fujian and the Yangtze delta: silk, porcelain and tea against a wall of imperial sea bans.

regions.name: Korea
regions.blurb: Joseon's coasts, closed to open foreign trade and reached through the Busan Waegwan and the Tsushima licence.

regions.name: Japan & the Ryukyus
regions.blurb: The silver islands: Nagasaki, Sakai and Osaka, and the Ryukyu kingdom's China-Japan entrepot trade.

regions.name: Caribbean & the Spanish Main
regions.blurb: Havana, Cartagena and Veracruz, the fortified convoy ports of the silver fleets, and the buccaneer islands.

regions.name: North America, Atlantic Coast
regions.blurb: The cod banks, the beaver rivers and the young English, Dutch and French colonies from Florida to Newfoundland.

regions.name: South America, Atlantic Coast
regions.blurb: Brazil's sugar captaincies and dyewood coast, and the Rio de la Plata's contraband road to Potosi.

regions.name: Pacific Americas
regions.blurb: Callao, Panama and Acapulco: the Peruvian silver route and the American end of the Manila galleon.

regions.name: Oceania & the Far Pacific
regions.blurb: The sandalwood islands of Timor, the galleon waypoint at Guam, and the still-uncharted southern continent.
